## Medicare Part A — Hospital Insurance (2026)
Medicare Part A covers inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facility care (up to 100 days per benefit period), hospice care, and some home health services. Most people qualify for premium-free Part A if they or their spouse paid Medicare taxes for at least 40 quarters.
- 2026 Premium: $0 for most beneficiaries
- 2026 Deductible: $1,736 per benefit period
- Days 61-90 coinsurance: $434 per day
- Lifetime reserve days (91+): $868 per day
- Skilled nursing facility coinsurance (days 21-100): $217 per day

## Medicare Part B — Medical Insurance (2026)
Medicare Part B covers doctor visits, outpatient surgery, preventive care, lab tests, X-rays, MRIs, mental health services, durable medical equipment, and ambulance services.
- 2026 Standard premium: $202.90 per month
- 2026 Annual deductible: $283
- Coinsurance: 20% of Medicare-approved amount (no annual cap on Original Medicare)

## Medicare Part C — Medicare Advantage (2026)
Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) is an all-in-one alternative to Original Medicare offered by private insurance companies approved by Medicare. Plans bundle Part A, Part B, and usually Part D into one plan. Many include extra benefits like dental, vision, hearing, fitness programs, over-the-counter allowances, and transportation.
- Many $0 premium plans available in Tennessee
- You must have Parts A and B to enroll
- Plans may be HMO, PPO, or PFFS
- Annual out-of-pocket maximum is required (unlike Original Medicare)
- Plan availability is defined county by county and changes every plan year

## Medicare Part D — Prescription Drug Coverage (2026)
Medicare Part D covers prescription medications through private insurance companies.
- 2026 Maximum deductible: $615
- 2026 Annual out-of-pocket cap: $2,100
- Late enrollment penalty: 1% of national base beneficiary premium per month without creditable coverage (permanent)

## Medigap Plan G vs. Plan N in Tennessee
Plan G and Plan N are the two most popular Medicare Supplement plans in Tennessee.

### Plan G (Most Popular — Maximum Coverage)
- Covers Part A coinsurance and hospital costs (up to 365 additional days)
- Covers Part B coinsurance/copayment at 100%
- Covers blood (first 3 pints)
- Covers skilled nursing facility coinsurance (days 21-100)
- Covers Part A deductible ($1,736)
- Does NOT cover Part B deductible ($283 per year — you pay this)
- Covers Part B excess charges at 100%
- Covers foreign travel emergency at 80%
- Best for: People who want maximum predictability and minimal out-of-pocket costs

### Plan N (Lower Premium — Small Copays)
- Same as Plan G except:
- Part B coinsurance has up to $20 copay per office visit
- Up to $50 copay for ER visits not resulting in admission
- Does NOT cover Part B excess charges
- Lower monthly premiums than Plan G (typically $30-$60 less)
- Best for: Healthy people who don't visit doctors frequently

## IRMAA 2026 — Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount
IRMAA is a surcharge on Medicare Part B and Part D premiums for higher-income beneficiaries. It is based on modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) from the tax return filed two years prior. The 2026 IRMAA is based on the 2024 tax return.

| Individual MAGI | Joint MAGI | Part B Monthly Premium | Part D Monthly Surcharge |
|---|---|---|---|
| ≤ $109,000 | ≤ $218,000 | $202.90 | $0.00 |
| $109,001-$137,000 | $218,001-$274,000 | $284.10 | +$14.50 |
| $137,001-$171,000 | $274,001-$342,000 | $405.80 | +$37.40 |
| $171,001-$205,000 | $342,001-$410,000 | $527.50 | +$60.30 |
| $205,001-$500,000 | $410,001-$750,000 | $649.20 | +$83.20 |
| Above $500,000 | Above $750,000 | $689.90 | +$91.00 |

Key IRMAA facts: Two-year lookback (2024 return determines 2026 premiums). Cliff effect — $1 over a threshold triggers full surcharge. Both spouses pay if filing jointly. You can appeal with Form SSA-44 for life-changing events. Applies to Medicare Advantage plans too.

## Medicare Late Enrollment Penalties
### Part B Penalty
If you don't enroll in Part B when first eligible and don't have qualifying employer group health coverage (COBRA and Marketplace/ACA do NOT count), you face a permanent penalty of 10% of the standard premium for each full 12-month period you could have had Part B but didn't. This penalty is added to your monthly Part B premium for as long as you have Medicare.

### Part D Penalty
If you go 63 or more consecutive days without Part D or other creditable prescription drug coverage after your Initial Enrollment Period, you face a permanent penalty of 1% of the national base beneficiary premium multiplied by the number of months without coverage.

### How to Avoid Penalties
- Part B: Enroll during your IEP around age 65, or maintain qualifying employer group coverage
- Part D: Enroll when first eligible or maintain creditable drug coverage (employer, VA, TRICARE)

## Medicare Enrollment Periods
1. Initial Enrollment Period (IEP): 7-month window around your 65th birthday (3 months before, birthday month, 3 months after)
2. Annual Enrollment Period (AEP): October 15 through December 7 each year
3. Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (OEP): January 1 through March 31
4. General Enrollment Period (GEP): January 1 through March 31 (coverage starts July 1)
5. Special Enrollment Periods (SEP): Triggered by qualifying life events (moving, losing employer coverage, Medicaid eligibility)

## Tennessee Medicaid (TennCare) and Medicare Savings Programs
Tennessee's Medicaid program is TennCare, administered by the state's Division of TennCare. The Medicare Savings Programs (QMB, SLMB, QI) can pay some or all of a beneficiary's Part B premium and, for QMB, cost-sharing as well. Qualifying automatically confers Extra Help with Part D costs. Income and resource limits change annually. Applications go through TennCare Connect (tenncareconnect.tn.gov).

## Veterans and Medicare
TRICARE For Life requires Medicare Parts A and B — skip Part B and you lose TFL. VA healthcare alone is not creditable coverage for Part B purposes. Darin Weidauer is a 22-year USAF veteran who understands how military benefits interact with Medicare, including for the large military and veteran community around Fort Campbell near Clarksville.
